title: SandboxSecurityAttestation
description: Evidence that a deployment's sandbox enforces the controls the control plane requires before it will authorize any execution. This is the bridge between two modules that deliberately cannot see each other: the hostile-execution gate holds container-runtime access and lives in services/runner, and the control plane is build-guarded against depending on it. The gate's verdict therefore travels as this document rather than as a method call. It is emphatically NOT a boolean: a passing attestation must enumerate every mandatory control and its verdict, so absence of a control is absence of evidence rather than a silent pass, and adding a control to the runner invalidates every existing attestation until a fresh assessment is produced. It also carries an OPTIONAL egressControls set, required only before an ALLOWLIST execution is authorized. No API accepts one — it arrives as deployment configuration — so nothing that authenticates to the control plane can assert its own security posture.

securityProfileVersion.description: Which sandbox security profile was assessed. An assessment for a different profile describes a different boundary and is refused.

probeImageDigest.description: The content address of the probe image the assessment ran. A tag would be a mutable pointer to executable code.

runtime.description: The container runtime the assessment ran against. Recorded and covered by the digest, but NOT currently compared against anything by the control plane — there is no configured expected runtime to compare it to. It is provenance for a human reading an audit trail, not a check, and this description says so rather than implying enforcement that does not exist.

assessedAt.description: When the assessment was taken. Freshness is enforced against database time, because this describes a running host rather than a source tree: a host reconfigured after the assessment is not described by it.

mandatoryControls.description: Every mandatory control and its verdict. The control plane requires EXACT set equality against the controls it independently demands, in both directions: containment would let a truncated assessment pass by omitting the control it failed, and would let a build accept an assessment produced for a weaker control set.

digest.description: A canonical semantic digest over this document's content, recomputed on load rather than trusted, so a document whose verdicts were edited does not keep the digest that described what it used to say.

egressControls.description: Whether this deployment can enforce a destination allowlist, control by control. OPTIONAL, and its absence is meaningful: an assessment that makes no egress claim is refused for an ALLOWLIST execution and is entirely unaffected for a DENY_ALL one. That is why it is a separate set from mandatoryControls rather than more entries in it — the two are demanded under different conditions, and requiring these of a run that wants no network would make it depend on a subsystem it does not use. Within its own scope the same exact-set-equality rule applies, and every control must PASS.
